did_you_know.text: Did you know? At the beginning of the chapter, Solomon is described as growing stronger in his kingdom, and the text attributes his success to the fact that the LORD his God was with him and made him exceedingly great.
Did you know? Solomon and the entire assembly went to Gibeon because the Tent of Meeting that Moses had made in the wilderness was there.
Did you know? The Ark of God was not in Gibeon. David had brought it up from Kiriath-jearim and placed it in a tent in Jerusalem, while the Tent of Meeting remained in Gibeon.
Did you know? Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings to the LORD on the bronze altar at Gibeon.
Did you know? After the burnt offerings had been offered, God appeared to Solomon during the night and said to him, “Ask what I should give you.”
Did you know? Solomon did not ask for wealth or victory over his enemies, but for wisdom and knowledge so that he could judge and lead the great people entrusted to him.
Did you know? According to the chapter, God granted Solomon's request because he had chosen wisdom and knowledge rather than wealth, honor, revenge on his enemies, or a long life.
Did you know? In addition to wisdom and knowledge, Solomon was also promised wealth, possessions, and honor—more than any king before him had possessed or any king after him would possess.
Did you know? Solomon had 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen. Some were stationed in the chariot cities, while others remained with the king in Jerusalem.
Did you know? After establishing himself as king, Solomon decided to build a house for the name of the LORD, as well as a house for his kingdom—that is, a royal palace.
